target_customer: Men who want to rent luxury and streetwear clothing and sneakers instead of buying
problem: Hyped streetwear and luxury pieces are expensive for the number of times they are worn, and men had few rental options.
business_model: Rental subscription and per item daily rental

founders.name: Travis Ezidiegwu
founders.background_notes: Named in Glossy April 2019 and on the YC page. No bio found in opened sources.

founders.name: Chike Achebe
founders.background_notes: Named in Glossy April 2019 and on the YC page.

founders.name: Tyreek Griffith
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page only.

competitors.name: Rent the Runway
competitors.what: Category leader in fashion rental, women focused
competitors.traction_then: Described as valued at 1 billion dollars
competitors.funding_then: Valued at about 1 billion dollars per Glossy

competitors.name: Rotarity
competitors.what: Streetwear rental service founded by Chris Hasek-Watt
competitors.traction_then: Named as the other notable streetwear rental service

competitors.name: Black Tux
competitors.traction_then: Described by the founders as near Rent the Runway scale but renting one item type

competitors.name: Seasons
competitors.what: Men's luxury and streetwear rental subscription in New York
competitors.traction_then: Launched Nov 2019 with 600 products and 50 members
competitors.funding_then: Initialized Capital, BoxGroup, WndrCo, Kindred Ventures, Notation Capital, amount undisclosed

technical_complexity.rationale: A storefront plus logistics for shipping, laundering and returns. The hard parts were operational, not technical.

defensibility.rationale: Inventory is bought from public brands and rental logistics were copyable. Glossy April 2019 and January 2020 coverage shows rivals and retailer in-house programs launching in the same window.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Glossy January 2020 reports Banana Republic, Vince and American Eagle launched in house rental programs within the prior year, while Rent the Runway's COO had no immediate interest in men's rental.

market_need_then: Glossy April 2019 describes demand for same day access to dropped streetwear. Men's rental was an emerging category with multiple entrants in 2019 and 2020.

identity.visual_style: Streetwear and luxury positioning, custom shipping box

branding.brand_signature: The 'Rent the Runway for men' framing

brand_strength.rationale: Launch coverage in Glossy April 2019 was the only press found. The club name is generic and no community, merch or fan evidence was found.

outcome_analysis: The Mercer Club launched in April 2019, entered YC Winter 2020 with a 150K seed reported by one database and is marked inactive by YC. No post-mortem, shutdown notice or later funding is public, so the cause is not public and failure factors stay empty. The category was crowded with Seasons, Rotarity and retailer programs, and COVID began just after the batch.
notes: No company website is listed and none was found. The seed round rests on a single database (CB Insights, 150K, 2020-03-17, YC); it is the standard YC deal. Village.ai claims the company came out of the Harvard Innovation Lab, an aggregator claim not confirmed. YC page lists three founders while team size is 2. Competitor Rotarity is spelled as Glossy gives it. Shutdown cause not public.
